title: [NPU] Skip fused gmm1+swiglu for swiglu_limit (SiLU-with-clamp) checkpoints (#40438)
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #39881. The fused gmm1 kernel ( npu_grouped_matmul_swiglu_quant_v2 ) applies plain SiLU with no clamp , but _uses_fused_gmm1 selected it for W4A8 MXFP4 MoE based only on the kernel type and use_fused_gmm1 — it never looked at the activation configuration.

Checkpoints whose MoE activation is SiLU-with-clamp ( swiglu_limit , e.g. DSV4) therefore lost the clamp when the fused kernel was selected, producing incorrect numerics. This silently bypassed the clamp path ( NPUSwigluMxfp8Quant ) that #38420 had just added for exactly this case.

## Modifications

Single-file change in python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/ascend.py :

- _uses_fused_gmm1(kernel, config) now takes the runner config and returns False when config.swiglu_limit is set and > 0 :
  - W4A8 MXFP4 + swiglu_limit (DSV4): falls back to the unfused path — w13 gmm + NPUSwigluMxfp8Quant(config.swiglu_limit) , which applies the clamp. This restores the pre-#39881 behavior
  - MXFP8 + swiglu_limit : raises NotImplementedError at init — this method has no unfused gmm1 path, so failing loudly beats silently serving wrong numerics (no known checkpoint hits this combination today)
  - Plain-SiLU models ( swiglu_limit unset or 0 ): keep the fused kernel, unchanged
- Both call sites ( __init__ and run() ) now pass the same config, so the activation selection and the fused/unfused branch decision can never disagree

## Accuracy Tests

- Dispatch logic verified locally with mocked kernels for all combinations: W4A8 ± swiglu_limit, MXFP8 ± swiglu_limit, use_fused_gmm1=False , and non-fused kernels — all resolve as intended
- DSV4 on NPU (fp4 experts → NPUW4A8MXFP4MoEMethod , swiglu_limit from HF config) now resolves to the unfused clamp path, bit-identical to the pre-#39881 serving path

## Speed Tests and Profiling

None — this PR intentionally trades the #39881 fusion gain back for correctness on clamp checkpoints. Plain-SiLU models (e.g. Kimi-K3 MXFP4) keep the full fused-path benefit (~15% per-layer MoE latency reduction from #39881). Recovering the fusion gain for clamp checkpoints would require adding a limit parameter to the fused kernel, which is kernel-side work out of scope here.

title: [AMD] Small-M MXFP4 fused-MoE kernel for gfx950 (Qwen) (#40204)
body:
## Motivation

For decode batches of 1 to ~40 tokens per rank, the MXFP4 MoE is the biggest cost per step on MI355X, and AITER
`fused_moe` only uses a small part of the HBM bandwidth there. This PR adds a HIP kernel pair for these shapes; above 40 tokens AITER is still used.

## Modifications

- New `python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/smallm_moe_gfx950/` (`__init__.py`, `smallm_moe.hip`): built with `hipcc` on
  first use and launched through ctypes, no build-time or wheel change.
- Phase 1: gate/up GEMM per (expert slot, 16-column slice), FP4 expanded with `v_cvt_scalef32_pk_bf16_fp4`, MFMA
  16x16x32 bf16, `silu(g) * u` written as bf16. Phase 2: down GEMM per (token, 64-row slice) with `v_dot2_f32_bf16`,
  top-k weights applied in fp32.
- Uses AITER's existing weight and scale layouts, so loading and preprocessing are untouched. Activations stay bf16.
- `moe_runner/aiter.py`: one guarded call before `fused_moe`, taken for FP4x2 weights, bf16 hidden 4096, per-rank
  intermediate 256 (the TP4 shape), 10 or 11 slots, silu, `tok <= 40`, and none of `expert_mask` / `doweight_stage1` /
  bias / `a1_scale` / `no_combine` / `num_local_tokens`. Everything else is unchanged. The TP2 shape (intermediate 512)
  crosses over to AITER much earlier (~20 tokens) and is left to a follow-up.
- On by default on gfx950; `SGLANG_ROCM_SMALLM_MOE=0` turns it off.
- Registered AMD unit test `test/registered/amd/test_smallm_moe_gfx950.py`: dequantized torch reference (rel L2 < 5e-3

## Motivation

Twenty-one MoE blocks repeat the same check before all-reducing their output over TP, and `should_skip_post_experts_all_reduce()` mixes two different questions in that check: whether the output still owes a sum at all, and whether a later step will run it. title: MiniMax-M3: MXFP8 dense-only block convert + aiter MXFP8 MoE on gfx950 (#36574)
body:
# MiniMax-M3: MXFP8 dense-only block convert + aiter MXFP8 MoE on gfx950

Branch: `m3/mxfp8-dense-block-convert` · base: `main` · **depends on #36559** (land it first) · `m3/fused-norm-fp8-quant` sits on top of this

> **Merge order:** #36559 must land before this PR. This PR's aiter MXFP8 MoE path passes `activation` through `fused_moe_kwargs`. On `main`, the aiter runner also passes `activation=` explicitly, so `fused_moe` raises `TypeError: got multiple values for keyword argument 'activation'`. #36559 pops it (`extra.pop("activation")`). Without #36559, this head reproduces the TypeError at graph capture on MI350X with `--moe-runner-backend aiter`.

MXFP8 checkpoints on gfx950 currently offer two all-or-nothing choices. Either every weight stays on the native MX per-1x32 `dot_scaled` path, or every weight is converted to block-fp8 `[128, 128]` at load (`SGLANG_FORCE_MXFP8_BLOCK_CONVERT`) and runs on the aiter block-scale kernels. Neither works for MiniMax-M3. The dense linears want the block-scale kernels, but converting the fused-MoE weights as well routes the MoE to a block-scale kernel that has no SwiGLU-OAI activation.

This PR adds four things:

- **`SGLANG_FORCE_MXFP8_BLOCK_CONVERT_DENSE`** (HIP only, default off). It converts only the MXFP8 dense linears to block-fp8. The fused-MoE weights stay MX per-1x32.
- **Small-M rowwise-fp8 path.** When the block-fp8 runner is `aiter_w8a8_block_fp8_linear` on gfx950, each converted dense layer also caches a rowwise-fp8 (per-token x per-channel) copy of its weight. At or below `MXFP8_DENSE_PTPC_DECODE_MAX_M = 128` tokens, the ptpc GEMM is used.
- **aiter MXFP8 MoE.** MXFP8 MoE weights are pre-shuffled with `shuffle_weight_a16w4` / `shuffle_scale_a16w4` and run through the aiter `PER_1X32` path with SwiGLU-OAI (`GateMode.INTERLEAVE`). Any `gemm1_alpha` other than 1.702 is rejected with `NotImplementedError`.
- **Making that MoE path reachable.** `_moe_runner_backend_quant_constraints` used to override `--moe-runner-backend aiter` to triton for every MXFP8 model. On gfx950 it now keeps `aiter` when `SGLANG_USE_AITER` is set; `maybe_get_hip_aiter_quant_info` builds nothing without aiter. Without aiter the request still falls back to triton. - **CUDA is unaffected.** Every new path is gated on `_is_hip`, `_is_gfx95_supported` or `_use_aiter`, or on the new env var.

title: MoE: small-batch sorting path with fused mxfp8 quantisation (#36559)
body:
# MoE: single-launch small-batch sorting with fused mxfp8 activation quant

aiter's opus MoE sorting kernel is sized for thousands of tokens; at decode batch sizes it
costs roughly 7us/layer of launch and ramp overhead, and the separate
`fused_dynamic_mxfp8_quant_moe_sort` stage1 activation quant costs another ~4us on top. When
the number of routing pairs `P = M * topk` is at most 64, the whole sorting job — stable
sort-by-expert, per-expert block padding, the expert-id table, `num_valid`, and the `moe_buf`
zero-fill — fits into one small Triton program built on `P x P` rank compares, and the stage1
mxfp8 quant rides the same launch on dedicated CTAs that recompute the (cheap) pair math
rather than cross-CTA synchronizing. This is installed as three runtime patch points on the
`aiter.fused_moe` module namespace (`fused_moe`, `_moe_sorting_impl`,
`fused_dynamic_mxfp8_quant_moe_sort`), each falling back to the original aiter function
whenever the fast path does not apply, so a stock aiter install needs no changes; the patch is
applied lazily and idempotently from `AiterRunnerCore.__init__`, so nothing outside the aiter
MoE runner is affected. Two supporting changes ship in the same area: `sanitize_topk_ids`,
which lets the native gfx950 MXFP8 MoE skip its defensive `topk_ids` copy when expert
parallelism cannot produce a non-local id (see **Correctness**), and `aiter_swiglu_oai_limit`,
which recognizes the exact SwiGLU-OAI configuration that aiter's `ActivationType.Swiglu` bakes
in as compile-time constants (`alpha=1.702`, `(up + 1.0)`) so the bf16 aiter runner uses that
kernel instead of silently running plain SiLU — and, where the aiter CK bf16 fused-MoE has no
SwiGLU-OAI codegen at all, so that `UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod` reports *why* the layer is
unsupported and falls back to the Triton runner.

Everything here is behind ROCm/aiter gates. `moe_sorting_small.py` is reachable only through
`apply_aiter_small_moe_sort_patch()`, called from `AiterRunnerCore.__init__`. The
`sanitize_topk_ids` plumbing only reaches a live code path inside
`quant_info.use_mxfp8 and is_hip() and is_gfx95_supported()`, and its default value is `True`,
i.e. exactly today's behaviour for any caller that does not pass it. The `unquant.py` changes
sit entirely inside the existing `_use_aiter and ... and get_moe_a2a_backend().supports_aiter()`
block. The default CUDA path is unchanged.

Measured on 8x MI350X (gfx950), MiniMax-M3-MXFP8, TP8, 80k input / 600 output.

title: [Perf] Lazy-load built-in model definitions and nixl_ep at startup (#41061)
body:
## Motivation

Importing `sglang.srt.models.registry` eagerly imports every module under `sglang.srt.models` (over 200 model files, on the order of 10-20 s on a typical dev box) even when `SGLANG_EXTERNAL_MODEL_PACKAGE` points at an out-of-tree package that provides the model actually being served. `sglang.srt.layers.moe.token_dispatcher.nixl` likewise probes `nixl_ep` at module import time, which every server pays for whether or not NIXL EP is used. This PR defers both until they are needed, which cuts startup time for deployments that serve out-of-tree models.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/models/registry.py`
  - When `SGLANG_EXTERNAL_MODEL_PACKAGE` is set, the registry starts with only the external package's models and imports the built-in package on the first lookup that needs it: `get_supported_archs()`, `register()`, or a `resolve_model_cls()` whose first architecture is not already registered. The merged view keeps the external models as overrides, exactly as `register(external_pkg, overwrite=True)` did.
  - Without the environment variable nothing changes: the built-in models are registered at import time as before.
  - New `is_arch_supported(arch)`, which answers from the already-registered models before falling back to the full set.
- `python/sglang/srt/model_loader/utils.py`: `get_model_architecture()` uses `is_arch_supported()` so that checking an external architecture does not trigger the built-in import.
- `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/nixl.py`: `nixl_ep` is imported inside a cached `_load_nixl_ep()` helper called from `NixlEPBuffer.get_buffer()` and the dispatcher constructor. A missing `nixl_ep` raises the same `ImportError` message at first use instead of at import time, and `topk_idx_t` is resolved there and stored on the dispatcher instance instead of a module global.
- `test/registered/unit/models/test_model_registry.py` (new, CPU suite, not part of the original commit): an external architecture resolves without importing the built-in package; the built-in package is imported exactly once when a built-in architecture is requested; external models still override built-ins after that import; `register()` still detects duplicates against the built-ins.

- `f3232c5d39`

title: [DeepEP v2] Let a model package supply its per-rank prefill dispatch bound (#41201)
body:
## Motivation

`validate_deepep_v2_dispatch_token_budget` compares the whole prefill-buffer ceiling (`--chunked-prefill-size` / `--max-prefill-tokens`) against `SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK`. A model package that scatters each prefill chunk over its attention-TP group before the MoE dispatch (sequence-parallel prefill under DP attention) sends only a fraction of that ceiling from any one rank, so the unsharded check rejects configurations that fit. For example, a 32768-token per-DP ceiling scattered over 8 attention-TP ranks dispatches 4096 tokens per rank.

The DeepEP v2 registry already lets an external model package declare its architecture and its MXFP8 precision policy. This extends that same entry point so the package can also declare how its prefill dispatch is sized, without SGLang core learning anything model-specific.

## Modifications

## Motivation

This PR fixes two cases where a layer's output was summed more than it should be when its FFN reduction runs later than the FFN.

1. **Replicated TP1 shared expert.** With `SGLANG_SHARED_EXPERT_TP1=1`, Laguna and `DeepseekV2MoE` (DeepSeek-V2/V3, GLM5-Next without MHC) replicate the shared expert on every TP rank and add its full output after the MoE all-reduce. 2. **Dense layers under DP attention reduce_scatterv.** Under DP attention with tp == dp == ep and no a2a backend, `postprocess_layer` reduce-scatterv'd every FULL-mode layer's output, whether or not the layer allows reduce-scatter.

   - A dense MLP leaves it out only under the published `mlp_reduce_scatter`, which needs `allow_reduce_scatter`. Without it, the MLP has already all-reduced, and the reduce-scatterv sums the output `tp_size` times.

title: [AMD] Honor an explicit triton moe_runner_backend for mxfp8 on ROCm (#41377)
body:
## Motivation

On ROCm, an explicit `--moe-runner-backend triton` with mxfp8 quantization is
silently discarded and the server fails to start.

`_moe_runner_backend_quant_constraints` adds `"triton"` to `allowed` only when
`is_gfx95_mxfp8`. On any other ROCm part the request falls through to the
`not in allowed` branch:

```
mxfp8 quantization supports only cutlass, deep_gemm, flashinfer_megamoe,
flashinfer_trtllm, flashinfer_trtllm_routed backends. Overriding 'triton'.
```

The substituted `flashinfer_trtllm` then reaches `flashinfer_trtllm.py
get_activation_type()`, whose unguarded `from flashinfer.fused_moe.core import
ActivationType` raises `ModuleNotFoundError` — flashinfer is not available on
ROCm.

Neither existing escape hatch can recover, because both run *after* the gate has
already pinned a non-auto value:

- the AMD early-return in `fp8.py` requires `runner_backend.is_aiter()`
- `create_moe_runner`'s ROCm fallback only fires `if moe_runner_backend.is_auto()`

And since this is a `@register_post_process` hook, it runs after model overrides
and clobbers `model_overrides/minimax_m3.py`'s own `moe_runner_backend = "triton"`.

This is not gfx1250-specific. `is_gfx95_supported()` matches only the substring
`"gfx95"`, so **gfx942 (MI300X / MI325X) is affected identically**. Verified on an
MI300X: `gcnArchName = gfx942:sramecc+:xnack-` → `is_gfx95_supported() == False` →
an explicit `--moe-runner-backend triton` resolves to `flashinfer_trtllm`. With the
fix, the same node resolves `triton` → `triton`, while `auto` → `flashinfer_trtllm`
and an unsupported name → `flashinfer_trtllm` are unchanged.

The fix keys on `get_platform().is_hip` rather than any single arch, so it covers
gfx942, gfx1250, and every other ROCm part at once, with no per-chip check to
maintain.

## Modifications

Widen `allowed` when an explicit `triton` request arrives on any ROCm part. Every
other entry in `MXFP8_MOE_RUNNER_BACKEND_CHOICES` is CUDA-only, so `triton` is the
only selectable runner there.

```python
if is_gfx95_mxfp8 or (get_platform().is_hip and moe_runner_backend == "triton"):
    allowed.append("triton")
```

Two deliberate limits:

- **`mxfp8_default` is untouched.** `auto` still resolves exactly as before on
  every platform, so nothing changes for anyone who does not ask for `triton` by
  name. The fix only stops the gate discarding an explicit request.
- **The `aiter` branch stays gated on gfx95**, since its MoE quant info is built
  only there.

`select_experts` already computes `num_fused_shared_experts_for_gate` — `0` on the per-rank fused shared-slot / aiter path, because the shared expert is appended afterwards by `_post_process_topk_ids` — and uses it at the **non-grouped** gate call sites. But the two **grouped** call sites (`grouped_topk` / `biased_grouped_topk`) still pass the raw `num_fused_shared_experts`, so on the per-rank fused shared-slot path the gate double-emits the shared marker:

- a routed expert is dropped — the gate is asked for `K_routed = top_k - num_fused_shared_experts` and spends one of those slots on its own marker (top-6 → top-5); and
- that marker lands at id `num_experts`, which the DeepEP per-rank remap shifts one past the end of the expert space (`384 → 392` on EP8, valid ids `0..391`).

DeepSeek-V4 routes through grouped `biased_grouped_topk`, so it hits this path. On the FlyDSL MegaMoEv2 backend (#35619) the out-of-range id faults the dispatch with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_EXCEPTION 0x1016` — which is exactly why #35619 has to run with `--disable-shared-experts-fusion`, forcing the shared expert to run as a separate per-layer GEMM instead of being fused into the megamoe dispatch/combine chain.

## What changed

* `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py`: pass `num_fused_shared_experts_for_gate` (not `num_fused_shared_experts`) to `grouped_topk` and `biased_grouped_topk` in `select_experts`.

Two lines. No-op off the per-rank fused shared-slot / aiter path (there `num_fused_shared_experts_for_gate == num_fused_shared_experts`). No behavior change on CUDA / non-fused-shared-slot paths.

## Validation (MI355X gfx950, DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813, TP8 / DP8 attention / EP8, `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe`)

With the fix, `--enforce-shared-experts-fusion` boots and serves — no `0x1016`; the dispatch/combine runs at `topk=7, local_experts=49` (48 routed + 1 fused shared per rank), confirming the shared expert is fused into the megamoe chain rather than run as a separate GEMM.

| shared-off (`--disable-shared-experts-fusion`) | 0.940 | 0.000 |
| shared-on (`--enforce-shared-experts-fusion`) | **0.970** | 0.000 |

title: [AMD] [GLM5] Fuse shared expert into AITER MoE on gfx950 (#41161)
body:
## Motivation

GLM-5.3-Flash has 288 routed experts and one always-on shared expert. The current AITER path executes routed `E=288, topk=8` MoE, then launches the shared gate/up projection, clamped SiLU and quantization, shared down projection, and a BF16 routed-plus-shared add separately.

This change appends the shared expert as expert ID 288 and dispatches one `E=289, topk=9` AITER MoE operation. The appended expert always has weight 1.0 because AITER already folds `routed_scaling_factor` into the routed weights.

The required gfx950 tuning dependency is merged in [ROCm/aiter#5735](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5735).

## Modifications

- Admit HIP shared-expert fusion only for AITER on gfx950, TP4 or TP8, `moe_ep_size == 1`, and no MoE A2A backend.
- Require GLM-5.3-Flash's validated geometry: hidden size 4096, MoE intermediate size 2048, 288 routed experts, routed top-k 8, one shared expert, and clamped SiLU G1U1.
- Require serialized dynamic 128x128 block-FP8 for both routed and shared experts; mixed layouts keep the separate path.
- Load the shared gate/up/down checkpoint tensors into appended expert ID 288 and expand routing from top-k 8 to top-k 9 with shared weight 1.0.
- Preserve existing CUDA behavior and the `--disable-shared-experts-fusion` rollback. No environment variable is added.
- Add admission/fallback, weight-loading, scaling, idle-batch, gfx950 component, and CUDA-graph replay coverage.

Disable with:

```bash
--disable-shared-experts-fusion
```

## Accuracy Tests

Full GLM-5.3-Flash GSM8K, 1,319 examples, thinking enabled, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, and zero request errors:

| TP | E=288/topk=8 | E=289/topk=9 fused | Delta |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4 | 97.57% | 97.19% | -0.38 pp |
| 8 | 96.74% | 96.89% | +0.15 pp |

Both arms used identical settings per TP. TP8 used a 131,072-token context, 1,200 evaluator threads, and 4,096 maximum output tokens. Decode CUDA graphs were enabled for TP4 and TP8.

Component validation: **15 tests passed, 16 subtests passed**. Coverage includes the exact TP4/TP8 admission and fallback table, appended expert ID 288 weight loading, top-k 8 to 9 routing, AITER shared weight 1.0, empty batches, retained bucket boundaries through `M=16384`, finite output, fused-versus-separate numerical agreement, and CUDA-graph capture/replay.
